surface.cancel_state: NO — a cancel control message cannot preempt a queued or in-flight command today; the mechanisms that exist are all coarser. (1) P3.3 per-connection cancel_event: created per connection (websocket.py:435-440) and consulted ONLY inside iter_messages between recv ticks (websocket.py:103-124, checks at l.116/l.122) — but the recv loop is SERIAL: `self._handle_message(websocket, message, client_id)` at websocket.py:559 blocks until `self._handler.handle(command)` returns (l.664/689/775), so a cancel frame arriving mid-command waits behind it and cancel_event's only effect is ending the recv loop afterward. The event backs connection teardown (request_cancel l.343, request_cancel_all l.356, invoked by stop() at l.317), not per-command preemption. (2) Command-level kill verbs: render_farm_cancel/render_stop/render_processes/emergency_halt are classified read-only (handlers.py _READ_ONLY_COMMANDS, cited by the bypass at websocket.py:686-693) so on a SECOND connection (websockets sync serve: per-connection threads; accept-loop daemon thread websocket.py:298-300, per-conn _handle_client l.424) they skip the C5 _MUTATION_LOCK (handlers.py:518-520) and the resilience gates and can be received while another command is in flight — but render_stop itself marshals onto the main thread (handlers_render.py:1731-1733, 30s), and tops_cancel_cook goes through _run_in_main_thread_pdg (handlers_tops/_common.py:82, 60s), so even kill verbs queue behind a frozen main thread. (4) C4 zombie-abandon (main_thread.py:371-394 per verified context) makes a deferred payload a no-op ONLY if it hasn't started; a payload mid-fn() (including node.render) runs to completion. Nothing can kill code already executing on the main thread.

risks: Global scope: while Manual is on, the ARTIST's own interactive edits also stop cooking — everything dirties silently and a cook burst fires at restore (mechanism inherent to hou.updateMode, per SideFX Hom docs pinned at harness/notes/h22_compat_ledger.json:32123-32134). Worse, the user sees a stale viewport during the build: UI responsive, scene frozen — an 'interactivity illusion' that can read as a bug.

Leave-behind hazard: an exception or crash between set and restore without a finally leaves the WHOLE SESSION in Manual — silent 'my scene stopped cooking' state. Escape hatches: try/finally restore, snapshot prior mode via hou.updateModeSetting() first (both symbols verified EXISTS), mode is non-persisted session state so a Houdini restart also recovers it.

Undo-group interleave: if the sandwich is ever combined with event-loop pumping between chunks (to keep the UI responsive mid-build), any artist edit in that window lands inside an open hou.undos.group — vendor docstring 'ALL changes to Houdini are recorded as a single action on the undo stack' (22.0.397 hou.py:106531-106534, quoted in freeze-class1-recon-2026-08-01.md:31/:92) → one artist Ctrl+Z wipes SYNAPSE's build or vice versa; the recon disqualified exactly this pattern under its rule 3.

Does not fix the atomic case: a single long cook (Mantra/SOP cook, Karma render) is indivisible C++ — Manual mode only collapses N redundant INTERMEDIATE cooks during a build flood; recon E's third ground (freeze-class1-recon-2026-08-01.md:128) applies: 'the cooks themselves are atomic C++ with no sub-unit'.

Undo-scope asymmetry with chunking: the refuted alternative (chunking) collapsed on the /mcp path because the outer marshal sets _tls.on_main=True and inner hops run inline (main_thread.py:230-231 Fast path 1, per recon E) — the sandwich avoids this by making NO hops, but that also means one long main-thread occupation for the whole build; UI freeze duration is sum-of-mutations, not sum-of-cooks, so the win is bounded by how much of the flood time was redundant cooking (C1: 'needs-live-measurement').
